title.zh: 卷一 本紀第一 太祖一
title.raw: 卷一 本紀第一 太祖一 Volume 1 Annals 1: Taizu 1

sentences.zh: 本紀第一 太祖一

translations.literal: Annals 1, Taizu 1
translations.idiomatic: Annals 1: Taizu, Part One

sentences.zh: 太祖開天行道肇紀立極大聖至神仁文義武俊德成功高皇帝，諱元璋，字國瑞，姓朱氏。

translations.literal: Taizu, the Supreme Emperor who opened Heaven's way, established the founding era, set the cosmic pole, was supremely sage and divine, benevolent in culture and righteous in martial affairs, of outstanding virtue and successful accomplishment, taboo name Yuanzhang, style name Guorui, surname Zhu.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu, the Supreme Emperor who opened Heaven's way, established the founding era, and set the cosmic pole—supremely sage and divine, benevolent in culture and righteous in war, of outstanding virtue and successful accomplishment—was tabooed Yuanzhang, styled Guorui, and surnamed Zhu.

sentences.zh: 先世家沛，徙句容，再徙泗州。

translations.literal: His ancestors first dwelt in Pei, moved to Jurong, and moved again to Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: His family had first lived in Pei, then moved to Jurong, and moved again to Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 父世珍，始徙濠州之鐘離。

translations.literal: His father Shizhen first moved to Zhongli in Haozhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhu Shizhen later moved the family to Zhongli in Haozhou.

sentences.zh: 生四子，太祖其季也。

translations.literal: He bore four sons; Taizu was the youngest.
translations.idiomatic: He had four sons; Taizu was the youngest.

sentences.zh: 母陳氏，方娠，夢神授藥一丸，置掌中有光，吞之，寤，口餘香氣。

translations.literal: His mother, the Lady Chen, while pregnant dreamed a god gave her one pill; placed in her palm it had light; she swallowed it; on waking, fragrance remained in her mouth.
translations.idiomatic: His mother, Lady Chen, while pregnant dreamed that a god gave her a single pill; when she held it in her palm it glowed, and after she swallowed it she awoke with a sweet fragrance still on her lips.

sentences.zh: 及產，紅光滿室。

translations.literal: When she gave birth, red light filled the room.
translations.idiomatic: At his birth, red light filled the room.

sentences.zh: 自是夜數有光起，鄰里望見，驚以為火，輒奔救，至則無有。

translations.literal: From then on, at night light often arose; neighbors seeing it, startled thinking it fire, would run to rescue, but on arriving there was nothing.
translations.idiomatic: After that, lights often appeared at night; neighbors who saw them, thinking the house was on fire, would rush to help, only to find nothing when they arrived.

sentences.zh: 比長，姿貌雄傑，奇骨貫頂。

translations.literal: When he grew up, his appearance was heroic and outstanding, with strange bones running through the crown of his head.
translations.idiomatic: As he grew, his bearing was heroic and imposing, with an extraordinary bone ridge running along the crown of his head.

sentences.zh: 志意廓然，人莫能測。

translations.literal: His will was vast and open; no one could fathom him.
translations.idiomatic: His ambitions were vast and unfathomable; no one could read his mind.

sentences.zh: 至正四年，旱蝗，大飢疫。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhizheng, drought, locusts, great famine and pestilence.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of the Zhizheng reign, drought and locusts brought famine and plague on a vast scale.

sentences.zh: 太祖時年十七，父母兄相繼歿，貧不克葬。

translations.literal: Taizu was then seventeen; father, mother, and elder brother died in succession; poor, unable to bury them.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu was then seventeen; his parents and elder brother died one after another, and he was too poor to bury them properly.

sentences.zh: 裡人劉繼祖與之地，乃克葬，即鳳陽陵也。

translations.literal: A fellow townsman Liu Jizu gave him land, and so he was able to bury them—that is the Fengyang mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: A neighbor, Liu Jizu, gave him land so that he could bury them at last—the site that became the Fengyang mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 太祖孤無所依，乃入皇覺寺為僧。

translations.literal: Taizu, orphaned with none to rely on, then entered Huangjue Temple as a monk.
translations.idiomatic: Left alone with no one to depend on, Taizu entered Huangjue Temple and became a monk.

sentences.zh: 逾月，游食合肥。

translations.literal: After more than a month, he went begging food at Hefei.
translations.idiomatic: After a little more than a month he went out to beg for food around Hefei.

sentences.zh: 道病，二紫衣人與俱，護視甚至。

translations.literal: On the road he fell ill; two men in purple garments went with him and guarded him with utmost care.
translations.idiomatic: On the road he fell ill; two men dressed in purple went with him and watched over him with extraordinary care.

sentences.zh: 病已，失所在。

translations.literal: When the illness ended, they were nowhere to be found.
translations.idiomatic: When he recovered, they had vanished without a trace.

sentences.zh: 凡歷光、固、汝、潁諸州三年，復還寺。

translations.literal: In all he passed through the prefectures of Guang, Gu, Ru, and Ying for three years, then returned to the temple.
translations.idiomatic: He spent three years wandering through Guang, Gu, Ru, and Ying and other prefectures, then returned to the temple.

sentences.zh: 當是時，元政不綱，盜賊四起。

translations.literal: At that time Yuan government lacked discipline; bandits rose on every side.
translations.idiomatic: By then Yuan rule had lost its grip, and rebels sprang up everywhere.

sentences.zh: 劉福通奉韓山童假宋後起潁，徐壽輝僭帝號起蘄，李二、彭大、趙均用起徐，眾各數萬，並置將帥，殺吏，侵略郡縣，而方國珍已先起海上。

translations.literal: Liu Futong, supporting Han Shantong who falsely claimed descent from Song, rose in Ying; Xu Shouhui usurped an imperial title and rose in Qi; Li Er, Peng Da, and Zhao Junyong rose in Xu—each with tens of thousands, all set generals, killed officials, invaded and plundered commanderies and counties, while Fang Guozhen had already risen first on the sea.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Futong backed Han Shantong, who claimed Song descent, and rose in Ying; Xu Shouhui declared himself emperor at Qi; Li Er, Peng Da, and Zhao Junyong rose in Xu—each commanding tens of thousands of men, appointing generals, killing officials, and ravaging commanderies and counties—while Fang Guozhen had already taken to the sea before them.

sentences.zh: 他盜擁兵據地，寇掠甚眾。

translations.literal: Other bandits held troops and occupied territory; raiding and plundering were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Countless other marauders seized territory and preyed on the land.

sentences.zh: 天下大亂。

translations.literal: The realm was in great disorder.
translations.idiomatic: The empire fell into utter chaos.

sentences.zh: 十二年春二月，定遠人郭子興與其黨孫德崖等起兵濠州。

translations.literal: In the second month of spring in the twelfth year, Guo Zixing of Dingyuan with his comrades Sun Deya and others raised troops at Haozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of spring in the twelfth year, Guo Zixing of Dingyuan and his followers Sun Deya and others raised an army at Haozhou.

sentences.zh: 元將徹里不花憚不敢攻，而日俘良民以邀賞。

translations.literal: The Yuan general Chelibuhua feared and did not dare attack, but daily captured good common people to claim reward.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuan general Chelibuhua was afraid to attack them and instead seized innocent civilians every day to claim rewards for victories.

sentences.zh: 太祖時年二十四，謀避兵，卜於神，去留皆不吉。

translations.literal: Taizu was then twenty-four; planning to avoid the fighting, he divined before the god—both going and staying were inauspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu was then twenty-four; wishing to escape the fighting, he divined before the temple god, but both staying and leaving came back ill-omened.

sentences.zh: 乃曰：「得毋當舉大事乎？

translations.literal: He then said: "Could it be that I should undertake a great affair?
translations.idiomatic: He then said, "Does this mean I am meant to undertake a great enterprise?"

sentences.zh: 」卜之吉，大喜，遂以閏三月甲戌朔入濠見子興。

translations.literal: " Divination was auspicious; greatly pleased, on the first day of the intercalary third month, day jiaxu, he entered Haozhou and saw Zixing.
translations.idiomatic: When he cast lots again the omen was favorable. Overjoyed, on the first day of the intercalary third month, jiaxu, he entered Haozhou and presented himself to Guo Zixing.

sentences.zh: 子興奇其狀貌，留為親兵。

translations.literal: Zixing marveled at his appearance and kept him as a personal guard.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Zixing was struck by his appearance and kept him as a personal guard.

sentences.zh: 戰輒勝，遂妻以所撫馬公女，即高皇后也。

translations.literal: In battle he always won; Zixing therefore gave him in marriage the daughter of the fostered Lord Ma—that is the Empress Gao.
translations.idiomatic: He won every battle he fought, and Guo Zixing gave him in marriage the daughter of his foster father Lord Ma—who became Empress Gao.

sentences.zh: 子興與德崖齟齬，太祖屢調護之。

translations.literal: Zixing and Deya had friction; Taizu repeatedly mediated between them.
translations.idiomatic: When Guo Zixing and Sun Deya fell out, Taizu repeatedly mediated between them.

sentences.zh: 秋九月，元兵復徐州，李二走死，彭大、趙均用奔濠，德崖等納之。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of autumn, Yuan troops recovered Xuzhou; Li Er fled and died; Peng Da and Zhao Junyong fled to Haozhou; Deya and others received them.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of autumn Yuan forces retook Xuzhou; Li Er fled and died; Peng Da and Zhao Junyong fled to Haozhou, where Sun Deya and the others admitted them.

sentences.zh: 子興禮大而易均用，均用怨之。

translations.literal: Zixing treated Peng Da with courtesy but slighted Junyong; Junyong resented this.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Zixing honored Peng Da but looked down on Zhao Junyong, who took offense.

sentences.zh: 德崖遂與謀，伺子興出，執而械諸孫氏，將殺之。

translations.literal: Deya then plotted with him; when Zixing went out they seized him and put him in stocks at the Sun residence, intending to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Deya then conspired with Junyong; when Guo Zixing went out they seized him, shackled him at the Sun compound, and were about to kill him.

sentences.zh: 太祖方在淮北，聞難馳至，訴於彭大。

translations.literal: Taizu was then north of the Huai; hearing of the crisis he galloped there and appealed to Peng Da.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu was then north of the Huai; hearing of the danger he rode hard to Haozhou and appealed to Peng Da.

sentences.zh: 大怒，呼兵以行，太祖亦甲而擁盾，發屋出子興，破械，使人負以歸，遂免。

translations.literal: Greatly angered, Peng Da called out troops to go; Taizu also donned armor, took a shield, broke through the roof to bring Zixing out, broke the stocks, had men carry him back on their backs, and so he was saved.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Da flew into a rage and mustered troops to march; Taizu donned armor, took up a shield, broke through the roof to free Guo Zixing, broke his shackles, and had men carry him home on their backs—thus saving his life.

sentences.zh: 是冬，元將賈魯圍濠。

translations.literal: That winter the Yuan general Jia Lu besieged Haozhou.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the Yuan general Jia Lu besieged Haozhou.

sentences.zh: 太祖與子興力拒之。

translations.literal: Taizu and Zixing resisted him with all their strength.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu and Guo Zixing resisted the siege with all their strength.

sentences.zh: 十三年春，賈魯死，圍解。

translations.literal: In spring of the thirteenth year, Jia Lu died and the siege was lifted.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the thirteenth year Jia Lu died and the siege was raised.

sentences.zh: 太祖收里中兵，得七百人。

translations.literal: Taizu gathered local troops and obtained seven hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu recruited men from the neighborhood and raised seven hundred troops.

sentences.zh: 子興喜，署為鎮撫。

translations.literal: Zixing was pleased and appointed him pacification commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Zixing was delighted and appointed him pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 時彭、趙所部暴橫，子興弱，太祖度無足與共事，乃以兵屬他將，獨與徐達、湯和、費聚等南略定遠。

translations.literal: At that time Peng and Zhao's troops were violent and overbearing; Zixing was weak; Taizu judged there was no one worth serving with long; he therefore placed his troops under another commander and alone with Xu Da, Tang He, Fei Ju, and others marched south to seize Dingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Da's and Zhao Junyong's men were brutal and overbearing, and Guo Zixing was too weak; Taizu decided he could not serve under them for long. He left his troops with another commander and marched south with only Xu Da, Tang He, Fei Ju, and others to take Dingyuan.

sentences.zh: 計降驢牌寨民兵三千，與俱東。

translations.literal: He planned to reduce the Donkey Brand stockade militia of three thousand and march east with them.
translations.idiomatic: He planned to win over the three thousand militia of the Donkey Brand stockade and march east with them.

sentences.zh: 夜襲元將張知院於橫澗山，收其卒二萬。

translations.literal: By night he raided the Yuan commander Zhang at Hengjian Mountain and took his twenty thousand soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: By night he attacked the Yuan commander Zhang at Hengjian Mountain and absorbed his twenty thousand soldiers.

sentences.zh: 道遇定遠人李善長，與語，大悅，遂與俱攻滁州，下之。

translations.literal: On the road he met Li Shanchang of Dingyuan; speaking with him, he was greatly pleased and together they attacked Chuzhou and took it.
translations.idiomatic: On the march he met Li Shanchang of Dingyuan; after talking with him he was greatly pleased, and together they attacked and captured Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 是年，張士誠據高郵，自稱誠王。

translations.literal: That year Zhang Shicheng held Gaoyou and styled himself King Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: That year Zhang Shicheng held Gaoyou and proclaimed himself King Cheng.

sentences.zh: 十四年冬十月，元丞相脫脫大敗士誠於高郵，分兵圍六合。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter in the fourteenth year, the Yuan chancellor Toghto greatly defeated Shicheng at Gaoyou and divided troops to besiege Liuhe.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter in the fourteenth year the Yuan chancellor Toghto routed Zhang Shicheng at Gaoyou and detached forces to besiege Liuhe.

sentences.zh: 太祖曰：「六合破，滁且不免。

translations.literal: Taizu said: "If Liuhe falls, Chuzhou cannot escape.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu said, "If Liuhe falls, Chuzhou will not be spared."

sentences.zh: 」與耿再成軍瓦梁壘，救之。

translations.literal: " He marched with Geng Zaocheng's army to Walang stockade to rescue it.
translations.idiomatic: He marched with Geng Zaocheng's army to Walang stockade to relieve the siege.

sentences.zh: 力戰，衛老弱還滁。

translations.literal: Fighting fiercely, he escorted the old and weak back to Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After fierce fighting he escorted the old and weak back to Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 元兵尋大至，攻滁，太祖設伏誘敗之。

translations.literal: Yuan troops soon came in great force and attacked Chuzhou; Taizu set an ambush and lured them to defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan forces soon arrived in strength and attacked Chuzhou; Taizu laid an ambush and lured them into a rout.

sentences.zh: 然度元兵勢盛且再至，乃還所獲馬，遣父老具牛酒謝元將曰：「守城備他盜耳，奈何舍巨寇戮良民？

translations.literal: Yet judging the Yuan army's momentum strong and that it would come again, he returned the horses they had captured and had the elders prepare cattle and wine to thank the Yuan commander, saying: "We guarded the city only against other bandits—why abandon the great bandit to slaughter good people?
translations.idiomatic: Yet judging that the Yuan army was strong and would return, he sent back the horses they had taken and had the elders bring cattle and wine to thank the Yuan commander, saying, "We held the city only against other bandits—why leave the great rebel to butcher innocent people?"

sentences.zh: 」元兵引去，城賴以完。

translations.literal: " The Yuan army withdrew, and the city thereby was preserved intact.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuan army withdrew, and the city was spared.

sentences.zh: 脫脫既破士誠，軍聲大振，會中讒，遽解兵柄，江淮亂益熾。

translations.literal: Toghto having defeated Shicheng, his military fame greatly shook; then slander at court suddenly stripped him of command, and disorder along the Jiang-Huai grew fiercer still.
translations.idiomatic: After defeating Zhang Shicheng, Toghto's fame shook the land; then court intrigue suddenly stripped him of command, and chaos along the Jiang-Huai grew worse than ever.

sentences.zh: 十五年春正月，子興用太祖計，遣張天祐等拔和州，檄太祖總其軍。

translations.literal: In the first month of spring in the fifteenth year, Zixing used Taizu's plan and sent Zhang Tianyou and others to take Hezhou, ordering Taizu to command all the troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring in the fifteenth year Guo Zixing, following Taizu's plan, sent Zhang Tianyou and others to take Hezhou and ordered Taizu to command the whole force.

sentences.zh: 太祖慮諸將不相下，秘其檄，期旦日會廳事。

translations.literal: Taizu feared the generals would not submit to one another; he kept the order secret and set the next morning for a meeting in the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu feared the generals would not accept his authority, so he kept the order secret and summoned them to the hall the next morning.

sentences.zh: 時席尚右，諸將先入，皆踞右。

translations.literal: At that time seating still honored the right; the generals all entered first and sat on the right.
translations.idiomatic: Seating still honored the right in those days; the generals entered first and all took the right-hand seats.

sentences.zh: 太祖故後至，就左。

translations.literal: Taizu deliberately came late and sat on the left.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu deliberately arrived late and took a seat on the left.

sentences.zh: 比視事，剖決如流，眾瞠目不能發一語，始稍稍屈。

translations.literal: When he took up business, his judgments flowed like water; the crowd stared wide-eyed and could not utter a word, and only then did they gradually yield.
translations.idiomatic: When he presided over affairs his judgments flowed like water; the others stared in silence, unable to speak, and only then began to yield.

sentences.zh: 議分工甓城，期三日。

translations.literal: They discussed dividing the work of bricking the wall, with a deadline of three days.
translations.idiomatic: They agreed to divide the work of repairing the city wall, with three days to finish.

sentences.zh: 太祖工竣，諸將皆後。

translations.literal: Taizu finished on time; all the generals were late.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu finished on time; every other commander was late.

sentences.zh: 於是始出檄，南面坐曰：「奉命總諸公兵，今甓城皆後期，如軍法何？

translations.literal: Then he produced the order, sat facing south, and said: "By order I command all your troops—now the wall work is all late; what does military law say?
translations.idiomatic: Then he produced the order, sat facing south, and said, "By order I command all your troops. The wall work is overdue—what does military law require?"

sentences.zh: 」諸將皆惶恐謝。

translations.literal: " All the generals were terrified and apologized.
translations.idiomatic: The generals were terrified and apologized.

sentences.zh: 乃搜軍中所掠婦女縱還家，民大悅。

translations.literal: He then searched out women seized in the army and sent them home; the people were greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: He then searched out women the troops had seized and sent them home; the people rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 元兵十萬攻和，拒守三月，食且盡，而太子禿堅、樞密副使絆住馬、民兵元帥陳野先分屯新塘、高望、雞籠山以絕餉道。

translations.literal: A hundred thousand Yuan troops attacked He; after three months of defense food was nearly gone, while the crown prince Toghon, the associate privy councillor Banzhuma, and the militia commander Chen Yexian separately encamped at Xintang, Gaowang, and Jilong Mountain to cut the supply road.
translations.idiomatic: A hundred thousand Yuan troops besieged Hezhou; after three months food was nearly gone, while Crown Prince Toghon, Associate Privy Councillor Banzhuma, and militia commander Chen Yexian camped at Xintang, Gaowang, and Jilong Mountain to cut the supply routes.

sentences.zh: 太祖率眾破之，元兵皆走渡江。

translations.literal: Taizu led the crowd to defeat them; the Yuan troops all fled across the river.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu led his men to defeat them, and the Yuan forces fled across the river.

sentences.zh: 三月，郭子興卒。

translations.literal: In the third month Guo Zixing died.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Guo Zixing died.

sentences.zh: 時劉福通迎立韓山童子林兒於亳，國號宋，建元龍鳳。

translations.literal: At that time Liu Futong had welcomed and installed Han Shantong's son Lin'er at Bo, state title Song, reign title Longfeng.
translations.idiomatic: By then Liu Futong had installed Han Shantong's son Lin'er at Bo as emperor of Song, with the reign title Longfeng.

sentences.zh: 檄子興子天敘為都元帥，張天祐、太祖為左右副元帥。

translations.literal: He ordered Zixing's son Tianxu as supreme commander, Zhang Tianyou and Taizu as left and right deputy commanders.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Guo Zixing's son Tianxu supreme commander and Zhang Tianyou and Taizu left and right deputy commanders.

sentences.zh: 太祖慨然曰：「大丈夫寧能受制於人耶？

translations.literal: Taizu said with emotion: "Can a great man willingly be controlled by others?
translations.idiomatic: Taizu said with feeling, "Can a true man willingly serve under another?"

sentences.zh: 」遂不受。

translations.literal: " He therefore did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He refused the appointment.

sentences.zh: 然念林兒勢盛，可倚藉，乃用其年號以令軍中。

translations.literal: Yet considering Lin'er's power strong and usable as support, he nevertheless used his reign title to command the army.
translations.idiomatic: Yet because Lin'er's power was strong and might be useful, he still used the Song reign title to command his troops.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，常遇春來歸。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of summer Chang Yuchun came to submit.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer Chang Yuchun came over to his side.

sentences.zh: 五月，太祖謀渡江，無舟。

translations.literal: In the fifth month Taizu planned to cross the river but had no boats.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Taizu planned to cross the Yangzi but had no boats.

sentences.zh: 會巢湖帥廖永安、俞通海以水軍千艘來附，太祖大喜，往撫其眾。

translations.literal: It happened that the Chaohu commanders Liao Yong'an and Yu Tonghai came with a thousand vessels of naval troops to attach themselves; Taizu was greatly pleased and went to reassure their forces.
translations.idiomatic: Just then the Chaohu leaders Liao Yong'an and Yu Tonghai came with a fleet of a thousand ships; Taizu was overjoyed and went to win over their men.

sentences.zh: 而元中丞蠻子海牙扼銅城閘、馬場河諸隘，巢湖舟師不得出。

translations.literal: But the Yuan vice censor-in-chief Manzi Haiya held the passes at Tongcheng Sluice, Machang River, and other points, so the Chaohu fleet could not get out.
translations.idiomatic: But the Yuan vice censor-in-chief Manzi Haiya held Tongcheng Sluice, Machang River, and other choke points, so the Chaohu fleet could not break out.

sentences.zh: 忽大雨，太祖喜曰：「天助我也!」遂乘水漲，從小港縱舟還。

translations.literal: Suddenly great rain fell; Taizu rejoiced and said: "Heaven helps me!" He then rode the rising water, taking small channels with boats to return.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly a great rain fell; Taizu exclaimed, "Heaven is helping me!" and rode the flood through side channels back to safety with his boats.

sentences.zh: 因擊海牙於峪溪口，大敗之，遂定計渡江。

translations.literal: He then struck Haiya at Yuxi mouth and greatly defeated him, and so fixed the plan to cross the river.
translations.idiomatic: He then attacked Haiya at Yuxi mouth and routed him, and so settled on the plan to cross the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 諸將請直趨集慶。

translations.literal: The generals asked to march straight on Jiqing.
translations.idiomatic: The generals urged a direct march on Jiqing.

sentences.zh: 太祖曰：「取集慶必自採石始。

translations.literal: Taizu said: "To take Jiqing one must begin at Caishi.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu said, "To take Jiqing we must begin at Caishi."

sentences.zh: 採石重鎮，守必固，牛渚前臨大江，彼難為備，可必克也。

translations.literal: Caishi is a heavy strongpoint and its defense must be firm; Niuzhu faces the great river in front—the enemy will find it hard to prepare and it can surely be taken.
translations.idiomatic: Caishi is a major strongpoint and will be heavily defended, but Niuzhu lies open to the great river—they will be hard pressed to guard it, and we can surely take it."

sentences.zh: 」六月乙卯，乘風引帆，直達牛渚。

translations.literal: " On the day yimao of the sixth month he caught the wind, raised sails, and went straight to Niuzhu.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao day in the sixth month he caught the wind, raised sail, and went straight to Niuzhu.

sentences.zh: 常遇春先登，拔之。

translations.literal: Chang Yuchun climbed first and took it.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Yuchun led the assault and took it.

sentences.zh: 採石兵亦潰。

translations.literal: The Caishi troops also collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: The Caishi garrison also broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 緣江諸壘悉附。

translations.literal: All the river forts along the bank submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Every riverside fort along the bank submitted.

sentences.zh: 諸將以和州飢，爭取資糧謀歸。

translations.literal: The generals, because Hezhou was starving, contended to seize provisions and grain and planned to return.
translations.idiomatic: Because Hezhou was starving, the generals quarreled over supplies and wanted to turn back.

sentences.zh: 太祖謂徐達曰：「渡江幸捷，若舍而歸，江東非吾有也。

translations.literal: Taizu said to Xu Da: "Crossing the river we were fortunate to succeed—if we abandon this and return, the lands east of the river will not be ours.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu told Xu Da, "We were lucky to cross the river—if we abandon this ground and go back, everything east of the river will slip from our hands."

sentences.zh: 」乃悉斷舟纜，放急流中，謂諸將曰：「太平甚近，當與公等取之。

translations.literal: " He then cut all the boat cables and let them drift in the swift current, telling the generals: "Taiping is very near—we shall take it with you.
translations.idiomatic: He cut every mooring rope and let the boats drift down the swift current, telling his commanders, "Taiping is close—we will take it together."

sentences.zh: 」遂乘勝拔太平，執萬戶納哈出。

translations.literal: " He then took advantage of victory to seize Taiping and captured the ten-thousand-household Naha'er.
translations.idiomatic: Riding the momentum of victory he took Taiping and captured the ten-thousand-household commander Naha'er.

sentences.zh: 總管靳義赴水死，太祖曰：「義士也」，禮葬之。

translations.literal: Supervisor Jin Yi drowned himself; Taizu said: "A righteous man," and buried him with ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: The supervisor Jin Yi drowned himself; Taizu said, "A man of honor," and buried him with full rites.

sentences.zh: 揭榜禁剽掠。

translations.literal: He posted a proclamation forbidding plunder.
translations.idiomatic: He posted notices forbidding looting.

sentences.zh: 有卒違令，斬以徇，軍中肅然。

translations.literal: A soldier violated the order; he beheaded him as a warning, and the army became sternly disciplined.
translations.idiomatic: When a soldier broke the rule he beheaded him as an example, and discipline in the army became iron.

sentences.zh: 改路曰府。

translations.literal: He changed circuit to prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He converted the circuit administration into a prefecture.

sentences.zh: 置太平興國翼元帥府，自領元帥事，召陶安參幕府事，李習為知府。

translations.literal: He established the Taiping Xingguo wing commander-in-chief's headquarters, himself holding the commander-in-chief's affairs; he summoned Tao An to join the staff and appointed Li Xi prefect.
translations.idiomatic: He established the Taiping Xingguo wing headquarters and took command himself; he summoned Tao An to his staff and appointed Li Xi prefect.

sentences.zh: 時太平四面皆元兵。

translations.literal: At that time on all four sides of Taiping were Yuan troops.
translations.idiomatic: Taiping was then surrounded on every side by Yuan forces.

sentences.zh: 右丞阿魯灰、中丞蠻子海牙等嚴師截姑孰口，陳野先水軍帥康茂才以數萬眾攻城。

translations.literal: The right vice censor-in-chief Aruhui, the censor-in-chief Manzi Haiya, and others massed troops to block the Gushu crossing; Chen Yexian's naval commander Kang Maocai attacked the city with tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: The right vice censor-in-chief Aruhui, the censor-in-chief Manzi Haiya, and others massed troops at the Gushu crossing; Chen Yexian's naval commander Kang Maocai besieged the city with tens of thousands of men.

sentences.zh: 太祖遣徐達、鄧愈、湯和逆戰，別將潛出其後，夾擊之，擒野先，並降其眾，阿魯灰等引去。

translations.literal: Taizu sent Xu Da, Deng Yu, and Tang He to meet them in battle; another detachment stole out behind them; attacking from both sides they captured Yexian and also reduced his troops; Aruhui and the others withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu sent Xu Da, Deng Yu, and Tang He to meet them head-on while another column slipped behind them; attacking from both sides they captured Chen Yexian and won over his troops, and Aruhui and the others withdrew.

sentences.zh: 秋九月，郭天敘、張天祐攻集慶，野先叛，二人皆戰死，於是子興部將盡歸太祖矣。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of autumn Guo Tianxu and Zhang Tianyou attacked Jiqing; Yexian rebelled; both were killed in battle; then all of Zixing's former generals submitted to Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of autumn Guo Tianxu and Zhang Tianyou attacked Jiqing; Chen Yexian turned traitor and both died in battle; from then on all of Guo Zixing's former officers passed to Taizu.

sentences.zh: 野先尋 為民兵所殺，從子兆先收其眾，屯方山，與海牙掎角以窺太平。

translations.literal: Yexian soon was killed by militia; his nephew Zhao Xian gathered his troops and encamped at Fang Mountain, coordinating with Haiya to spy on Taiping.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yexian was soon killed by local militia; his nephew Zhao Xian gathered the remnant forces and camped at Fang Mountain, joining Haiya to threaten Taiping from two sides.

sentences.zh: 冬十二月壬子，釋納哈出北歸。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of winter, day renzi, he released Naha'er to return north.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi day in the twelfth month of winter he released Naha'er to return north.

sentences.zh: 十六年春二月丙子，大破海牙於採石。

translations.literal: In the second month of spring in the sixteenth year, day bingzi, he greatly defeated Haiya at Caishi.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi day in the second month of spring in the sixteenth year he routed Haiya at Caishi.

sentences.zh: 三月癸未，進攻集慶，擒兆先，降其眾三萬六千人，皆疑懼不自保。

translations.literal: On the day guiwei of the third month he advanced to attack Jiqing, captured Zhao Xian, and reduced his thirty-six thousand troops—all were fearful and did not feel secure.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei day in the third month he advanced on Jiqing, captured Zhao Xian, and absorbed his thirty-six thousand men, who were all fearful and uneasy.

sentences.zh: 太祖擇驍健者五百人入衛，解甲酣寢達旦，眾心始安。

translations.literal: Taizu selected five hundred of the fiercest and strongest to enter as guards; he removed armor and slept soundly until dawn, and the crowd's hearts then settled.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu picked five hundred of the sturdiest men for his personal guard, laid aside his armor, and slept soundly until dawn; only then did their minds ease.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，再敗元兵於蔣山。

translations.literal: On the day gengyin he again defeated Yuan troops at Jiang Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin day he defeated the Yuan army again at Jiangshan.

sentences.zh: 元御史大夫福壽，力戰死之，蠻子海牙遁歸張士誠，康茂才降。

translations.literal: The Yuan censor-in-chief Fushou fought to the death; Manzi Haiya fled back to Zhang Shicheng; Kang Maocai submitted.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuan censor-in-chief Fushou fought to the death; Manzi Haiya fled to Zhang Shicheng; Kang Maocai surrendered.

sentences.zh: 太祖入城，悉召官吏父老諭之曰：「元政氵賣擾，干戈蜂起，我來為民除亂耳，其各安堵如故。

translations.literal: Taizu entered the city and summoned all officials and elders to instruct them: "Yuan government is corrupt and disorder runs wild; arms rise like hornets—I have come to remove chaos for the people; each of you keep your homes in peace as before.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu entered the city and called in the officials and elders, telling them, "Yuan rule has collapsed into chaos and war swarms everywhere—I have come only to deliver the people from disorder. Go on living in peace as before."

sentences.zh: 賢士吾禮用之，舊政不便者除之，吏毋貪暴殃吾民。

translations.literal: For worthy men I will honor and employ them; what is inconvenient in old government I will remove; officials must not be greedy or violent and harm my people.
translations.idiomatic: Men of talent I shall honor and employ; harmful old practices I shall abolish; and officials must not prey on the people with greed or violence."

sentences.zh: 」民乃大喜過望。

translations.literal: " The people then rejoiced beyond expectation.
translations.idiomatic: The people rejoiced beyond anything they had hoped for.

sentences.zh: 改集慶路為應天府，辟夏煜、孫炎、楊憲等十余人，葬御史大夫福壽，以旌其忠。

translations.literal: He changed the Jiqing circuit to Yingtian Prefecture, recruited Xia Yu, Sun Yan, Yang Xian, and more than ten others, buried the censor-in-chief Fushou, and honored his loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: He renamed the Jiqing circuit Yingtian Prefecture, recruited Xia Yu, Sun Yan, Yang Xian, and more than a dozen others, buried Censor-in-Chief Fushou, and honored his loyalty.

sentences.zh: 當是時，元將定定扼鎮江，別不華、楊仲英屯寧國，青衣軍張明鑒據揚州，八思爾不花駐徽州，石抹宜孫守處州，其弟厚孫守婺州，宋伯顏不花守衢州，而池州已為徐壽輝將所據，張士誠自淮東陷平江，轉掠浙西。

translations.literal: At that time the Yuan general Dingding held Zhenjiang; Biebuhua and Yang Zhongying encamped at Ningguo; the Green-Clothes Army's Zhang Mingjian held Yangzhou; Basibuhua was stationed at Huizhou; Shimo Yisun guarded Chuzhou, his younger brother Housun guarded Wuzhou, Song Boyanbuhua guarded Quzhou, while Chizhou had already been seized by Xu Shouhui's general, Zhang Shicheng from east of the Huai had taken Pingjiang and turned to raid western Zhe.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Yuan generals held the land on every side: Dingding at Zhenjiang, Biebuhua and Yang Zhongying at Ningguo, Zhang Mingjian's Green-Clothes Army at Yangzhou, Basibuhua at Huizhou, Shimo Yisun at Chuzhou with his brother Housun at Wuzhou, Song Boyanbuhua at Quzhou, Chizhou already in the hands of Xu Shouhui's officer, and Zhang Shicheng, having overrun the Huai east, had seized Pingjiang and was raiding western Zhe.

sentences.zh: 太祖既定集慶，慮士誠、壽輝強，江左、浙右諸郡為所並，於是遣徐達攻鎮江，拔之，定定戰死。

translations.literal: Taizu having settled Jiqing, feared Shicheng and Shouhui strong, and that the commanderies of left Jiang and right Zhe would be swallowed by them; he therefore sent Xu Da to attack Zhenjiang and took it; Dingding died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Once Jiqing was secure, Taizu worried that Shicheng and Shouhui were too strong and would swallow the Jiang-left and Zhe-right commanderies, so he sent Xu Da against Zhenjiang; the city fell and Dingding died in battle.

sentences.zh: 夏六月，鄧 愈克廣德。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of summer Deng Yu took Guangde.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of summer Deng Yu captured Guangde.

sentences.zh: 秋七月己卯，諸將奉太祖為吳國公。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn, day jimao, the generals installed Taizu as Duke of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, on jimao day, his commanders proclaimed Taizu Duke of Wu.

sentences.zh: 置江南行中書省，自總省事，置僚佐。

translations.literal: He established the Jiangnan Branch Secretariat, himself presiding over affairs, and set up assistants.
translations.idiomatic: He established the Jiangnan Branch Secretariat, took charge of its affairs himself, and appointed a staff.

sentences.zh: 貽書張士誠，士誠不報，引兵攻鎮江。

translations.literal: He sent a letter to Zhang Shicheng; Shicheng did not reply and led troops to attack Zhenjiang.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote to Zhang Shicheng, who made no reply and instead marched on Zhenjiang.

sentences.zh: 徐達敗之，進圍常州，不下。

translations.literal: Xu Da defeated him and pressed the siege of Changzhou, which would not fall.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Da routed him and pressed the siege of Changzhou, which still held out.

sentences.zh: 九月戊寅，如鎮江，謁孔子廟。

translations.literal: On the day wuyin of the ninth month he went to Zhenjiang and visited the Temple of Confucius.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin day in the ninth month he went to Zhenjiang and paid his respects at the Temple of Confucius.

sentences.zh: 遣儒士告諭父老，勸農桑，尋還應天。

translations.literal: He sent Confucian scholars to announce and instruct the elders, encouraged farming and sericulture, and soon returned to Yingtian.
translations.idiomatic: He sent scholars to address the elders, urged farming and sericulture, and soon returned to Yingtian.

sentences.zh: 十七年春二月，耿炳文克長興。

translations.literal: In the second month of spring in the seventeenth year Geng Bingwen took Changxing.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of spring in the seventeenth year Geng Bingwen captured Changxing.

sentences.zh: 三月，徐達克常州。

translations.literal: In the third month Xu Da took Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Xu Da took Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 夏四月丁卯，自將攻寧國，取之，別不華降。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of summer, day dingmao, he personally led an attack on Ningguo and took it; Biebuhua submitted.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao day in the fourth month of summer he led the assault on Ningguo in person, took the city, and Biebuhua surrendered.

sentences.zh: 五月，上元、寧國、句容獻瑞麥。

translations.literal: In the fifth month Shangyuan, Ningguo, and Jurong presented auspicious wheat.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Shangyuan, Ningguo, and Jurong presented wheat with double ears—a propitious sign.

sentences.zh: 六月，趙繼祖克江陰。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Zhao Jizu took Jiangyin.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Zhao Jizu took Jiangyin.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，徐達克常熟。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn Xu Da took Changshu.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn Xu Da took Changshu.

sentences.zh: 胡大海克徽州，八思爾不花遁。

translations.literal: Hu Dahai took Huizhou; Basibuhua fled.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Dahai took Huizhou and Basibuhua fled.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，常遇春克池州，繆大亨克揚州，張明鑒降。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter Chang Yuchun took Chizhou; Miao Daheng took Yangzhou and Zhang Mingjian submitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter Chang Yuchun took Chizhou; Miao Daheng took Yangzhou and Zhang Mingjian surrendered.

sentences.zh: 十二月己丑，釋囚。

translations.literal: On the day jichou of the twelfth month he released prisoners.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou day in the twelfth month he released prisoners.

sentences.zh: 是年，徐壽輝將明玉珍據重慶路。

translations.literal: That year Xu Shouhui's general Ming Yuzhen held the Chongqing circuit.
translations.idiomatic: That year Xu Shouhui's general Ming Yuzhen held the Chongqing region.

sentences.zh: 十八年春二月乙亥，以康茂才為營田使。

translations.literal: In the second month of spring in the eighteenth year, day yihai, he appointed Kang Maocai camp-field commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai day in the second month of spring in the eighteenth year he appointed Kang Maocai commissioner of military colonies.

sentences.zh: 三月己酉，錄囚。

translations.literal: On the day jiyou of the third month he reviewed criminal cases.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou day in the third month he reviewed criminal cases.

sentences.zh: 鄧愈克建德路。

translations.literal: Deng Yu took Jiande circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Yu took Jiande.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，徐壽輝將陳友諒遣趙普勝陷池州。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of summer Xu Shouhui's general Chen Youliang sent Zhao Pusheng to seize Chizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer Chen Youliang, a general of Xu Shouhui, sent Zhao Pusheng to seize Chizhou.

sentences.zh: 是月，友諒據龍興路。

translations.literal: That month Youliang held Longxing circuit.
translations.idiomatic: That same month Youliang took Longxing.

sentences.zh: 五月，劉福通破汴梁，迎韓林兒都之。

translations.literal: In the fifth month Liu Futong took Bianliang and welcomed Han Lin'er to make it his capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Liu Futong captured Bianliang and moved Han Lin'er's court there.

sentences.zh: 初，福通遣將分道四齣，破山東，寇秦晉，掠幽薊，中原大亂，太祖故得次第略定江表。

translations.literal: Earlier Futong had sent generals in separate columns in four directions, broke Shandong, raided Qin and Jin, plundered You and Ji—the central plain was in great disorder, and so Taizu was able step by step to secure the lands along the river.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Liu Futong had sent armies in four directions, overrun Shandong, raided Qin and Jin, and plundered You and Ji until the central plain was in chaos—giving Taizu the opening to secure the Yangzi lands one by one.

sentences.zh: 所過不殺，收召才雋，由是人心日附。

translations.literal: Where he passed he did not kill; he gathered and summoned talented men—thereby hearts daily attached to him.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he marched he forbade slaughter and gathered men of talent, and day by day more hearts turned to him.

sentences.zh: 冬十二月，胡大海攻婺州，久不下，太祖自將往擊之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of winter Hu Dahai attacked Wuzhou; long unable to take it, Taizu personally led troops to strike.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of winter Hu Dahai besieged Wuzhou without success, and Taizu marched to take command in person.

sentences.zh: 石抹宜孫遣將率車師由松溪來援，太祖曰：「道狹，車戰適取敗耳。

translations.literal: Shimo Yisun sent a general leading chariot troops to aid from Songxi; Taizu said: "The road is narrow—chariot warfare is exactly what brings defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Shimo Yisun sent a relief column with war chariots from Songxi; Taizu said, "The road is narrow—chariots are a recipe for defeat."

sentences.zh: 」命胡德濟迎戰於梅花門，大破之，婺州降，執厚孫。

translations.literal: " He ordered Hu Deji to meet them in battle at Meihua Gate, greatly defeated them, Wuzhou submitted, and Housun was captured.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Hu Deji to meet them at Meihua Gate, routed them completely, took Wuzhou, and captured Housun.

sentences.zh: 先一日，城中人望見城西五色雲如車蓋，以為異，及是乃知為太祖駐兵地。

translations.literal: The day before, people in the city had seen west of the city five-colored clouds like a carriage canopy and thought it strange; only then did they know it was where Taizu had encamped.
translations.idiomatic: The day before, the townspeople had seen five-colored clouds like a carriage canopy west of the city and marveled; only now did they learn it marked the place where Taizu had camped.

sentences.zh: 入城，發粟振貧民，改州為寧越府。

translations.literal: Entering the city, he opened granaries to relieve the poor and changed the prefecture to Ningyue Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the city, opened the granaries to feed the poor, and renamed the prefecture Ningyue.

sentences.zh: 辟范祖干、葉儀、許元等十三人分直講經史。

translations.literal: He recruited Fan Zugan, Ye Yi, Xu Yuan, and thirteen others to lecture on the classics and histories in rotation.
translations.idiomatic: He recruited Fan Zugan, Ye Yi, Xu Yuan, and thirteen others to lecture on the classics and histories in shifts.

sentences.zh: 戊子，遣使招諭方國珍。

translations.literal: On the day wuzi he sent envoys to summon and instruct Fang Guozhen.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi day he sent envoys to summon Fang Guozhen to allegiance.

sentences.zh: 十九年春正月乙巳，太祖謀取浙東未下諸路。

translations.literal: In the first month of spring in the nineteenth year, day yisi, Taizu planned to take the routes of eastern Zhe not yet subdued.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi day in the first month of spring in the nineteenth year Taizu planned the conquest of the remaining routes in eastern Zhe.

sentences.zh: 戒諸將曰：「克城以武，戡亂以仁。

translations.literal: He warned the generals: "To take cities use force; to quell disorder use benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: He warned his commanders, "Take cities by force, but pacify disorder with humanity."

sentences.zh: 吾比入集慶，秋毫無犯，故一舉而定。

translations.literal: When I lately entered Jiqing I did not violate even a hair, and so one effort settled it.
translations.idiomatic: When I entered Jiqing I did not harm so much as a hair, and the city fell in a single stroke."

sentences.zh: 每聞諸將得一城不妄殺，輒喜不自勝。

translations.literal: Whenever I hear that a general has taken a city without reckless killing, I cannot contain my joy.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever I hear that a commander has taken a city without slaughter, I cannot contain my joy."

sentences.zh: 夫師行如火，不戢將燎原。

translations.literal: An army on the march is like fire—if not checked it will burn the plain.
translations.idiomatic: An army on the march is like fire unchecked—it will burn the plain."

sentences.zh: 為將能以不殺為武，豈惟國家之利，子孫實受其福。

translations.literal: For a general to be able to make not killing his martial virtue—is it not only the state's benefit? Descendants truly receive its blessing.
translations.idiomatic: A commander who makes restraint his weapon serves not only the state—his descendants will reap the blessing."

sentences.zh: 」庚申，胡大海克諸暨。

translations.literal: " On the day gengshen Hu Dahai took Zhuji.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen day Hu Dahai took Zhuji.

sentences.zh: 是月，命寧越知府王宗顯立郡學。

translations.literal: That month he ordered Ningyue Prefect Wang Zongxian to establish a prefectural school.
translations.idiomatic: That month he ordered Wang Zongxian, prefect of Ningyue, to establish a prefectural school.

sentences.zh: 三月甲午，赦大逆以下。

translations.literal: On the day jiawu of the third month he pardoned all below great treason.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu day in the third month he granted amnesty short of great treason.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，方國珍以溫、台、慶元來獻，遣其子關為質，不受。

translations.literal: On the day dingsi Fang Guozhen presented Wen, Tai, and Qingyuan; he sent his son Guan as hostage; Taizu did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi day Fang Guozhen offered Wen, Tai, and Qingyuan and sent his son Guan as a hostage; Taizu refused the hostage.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，俞通海等復池州。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of summer Yu Tonghai and others recovered Chizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer Yu Tonghai and others recovered Chizhou.

sentences.zh: 時耿炳文守長興，吳良守江陰，湯和守常州，皆數敗士誠兵。

translations.literal: At that time Geng Bingwen held Changxing, Wu Liang held Jiangyin, and Tang He held Changzhou—all several times defeated Shicheng's troops.
translations.idiomatic: Geng Bingwen held Changxing, Wu Liang Jiangyin, and Tang He Changzhou—each had beaten Shicheng's armies again and again.

sentences.zh: 太祖以故久留寧越，徇浙東。

translations.literal: Taizu therefore long remained at Ningyue and pacified eastern Zhe.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu therefore lingered at Ningyue while he secured eastern Zhe.

sentences.zh: 六月壬戌，還應天。

translations.literal: On the day renxu of the sixth month he returned to Yingtian.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu day in the sixth month he returned to Yingtian.

sentences.zh: 秋八月，元察罕帖木兒復汴梁，福通以林兒退保安豐。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of autumn the Yuan Chaghan Temür recovered Bianliang; Futong withdrew Lin'er to Bo'anfeng.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of autumn the Yuan general Chaghan Temür retook Bianliang and Liu Futong withdrew Han Lin'er to Bo'anfeng.

sentences.zh: 九月，常遇春克衢州，擒宋伯顏不花。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Chang Yuchun took Quzhou and captured Song Boyanbuhua.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Chang Yuchun took Quzhou and captured Song Boyanbuhua.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，遣夏煜授方國珍行省平章，國珍以疾辭。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter he sent Xia Yu to appoint Fang Guozhen branch secretariat pacification commissioner; Guozhen declined on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter he sent Xia Yu to offer Fang Guozhen the post of branch secretariat pacification commissioner; Guozhen pleaded illness and declined.

sentences.zh: 十一月壬寅，胡大海克處州，石抹宜孫遁。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, day renyin, Hu Dahai took Chuzhou and Shimo Yisun fled.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin day in the eleventh month Hu Dahai took Chuzhou and Shimo Yisun fled.

sentences.zh: 時元守兵單弱，且聞中原亂，人心離散，以故江左、浙右諸郡，兵至皆下，遂西與友諒鄰。

translations.literal: At that time Yuan garrison troops were few and weak, and hearing of disorder in the central plain hearts scattered; for this reason the commanderies of left Jiang and right Zhe, when troops arrived all submitted, and he thus bordered Youliang on the west.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan garrisons were thin and news of chaos in the north had broken their morale, so commandery after commandery in Jiang-left and Zhe-right fell as his armies approached, until he shared a western border with Youliang.

sentences.zh: 二十年春二月，元福建行省參政袁天祿以福寧降。

translations.literal: In the second month of spring in the twentieth year Yuan Fujian Branch Secretariat Associate Administrator Yuan Tianlu submitted Funing.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of spring in the twentieth year Yuan Tianlu, associate administrator of the Fujian Branch Secretariat, surrendered Funing.

sentences.zh: 三月戊子，征劉基、宋濂、章溢、葉琛至。

translations.literal: On the day wuzi of the third month he summoned Liu Ji, Song Lian, Zhang Yi, and Ye Chen to come.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi day in the third month he summoned Liu Ji, Song Lian, Zhang Yi, and Ye Chen to court.

sentences.zh: 夏五月，徐達、常遇春敗陳友諒於池州。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of summer Xu Da and Chang Yuchun defeated Chen Youliang at Chizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of summer Xu Da and Chang Yuchun defeated Chen Youliang at Chizhou.

sentences.zh: 閏月丙辰，友諒陷太平，守將硃文遜，院判花雲、王鼎，知府許瑗死之。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, day bingchen, Youliang took Taiping; the defending general Zhu Wensun, administrative vice commissioner Hua Yun and Wang Ding, and prefect Xu Yuan died for it.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen day in the intercalary month Youliang seized Taiping; the defender Zhu Wensun, Vice Commissioners Hua Yun and Wang Ding, and Prefect Xu Yuan were killed.

sentences.zh: 未幾，友諒弒其主徐壽輝，自稱皇帝，國號漢，盡有江西、湖廣地，約士誠合攻應天，應天大震。

translations.literal: Before long Youliang murdered his lord Xu Shouhui, styled himself emperor, state title Han, fully held Jiangxi and Huguang lands, and agreed with Shicheng to jointly attack Yingtian—Yingtian was greatly shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, Youliang murdered his master Xu Shouhui, declared himself emperor of Han, held all Jiangxi and Huguang, and joined Zhang Shicheng in a planned assault on Yingtian—the capital was thrown into alarm.

sentences.zh: 諸將議先復太平以牽之，太祖曰：「不可。

translations.literal: The generals discussed first recovering Taiping to pin him; Taizu said: "Cannot.
translations.idiomatic: His commanders urged recapturing Taiping first to pin Youliang down; Taizu said, "No."

sentences.zh: 彼居上游，舟師十倍於我，猝難復也。

translations.literal: He occupies the upper reaches; his naval forces are ten times ours—suddenly hard to recover.
translations.idiomatic: He holds the upper river; his fleet outnumbers ours ten to one—we cannot retake Taiping in a rush."

sentences.zh: 」或請自將迎擊，太祖曰：「不可。

translations.literal: " Some asked him to lead in person to meet the attack; Taizu said: "Cannot.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged him to lead the army out to meet them; Taizu said, "No."

sentences.zh: 彼以偏師綴我，而全軍趨金陵，順流半日可達，吾步騎急難引還，百里趨戰，兵法所忌，非策也。

translations.literal: He would use a detached force to detain us while his full army rushed Jinling—downstream half a day could reach; our infantry and cavalry urgently hard to pull back—a hundred li to rush to battle is what military law forbids; not a strategy.
translations.idiomatic: He would tie us down with a diversion while his main fleet raced for Jinling—half a day's sail downstream. Our foot and horse could not turn back in time; to fight a hundred li from home is what doctrine forbids."

sentences.zh: 」乃馳諭胡大海搗信州牽其後，而令康茂才以書紿友諒，令速來。

translations.literal: " He then galloped orders to Hu Dahai to strike Xinzhou in the rear to pull him, and ordered Kang Maocai with a letter to deceive Youliang and make him come quickly.
translations.idiomatic: He galloped orders to Hu Dahai to raid Xinzhou and threaten Youliang's rear, and had Kang Maocai lure him east with a forged letter.

sentences.zh: 友諒果引兵東。

translations.literal: Youliang indeed led troops east.
translations.idiomatic: Youliang took the bait and marched east.

sentences.zh: 於是常遇春伏石灰山，徐達陣南門外，楊璟屯大勝港，張德勝等以舟師出龍江關，太祖親督軍盧龍山。

translations.literal: Thereupon Chang Yuchun lay in ambush at Lime Mountain, Xu Da formed battle at the south gate, Yang Jing encamped at Dasheng Harbor, Zhang Desheng and others with naval forces issued from Longjiang Pass, and Taizu personally supervised the army at Lulong Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Yuchun hid at Lime Mountain, Xu Da formed line at the south gate, Yang Jing held Dasheng Harbor, Zhang Desheng and others took the fleet out through Longjiang Pass, and Taizu commanded in person from Lulong Mountain.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，友諒至龍灣，眾欲戰，太祖曰：「天且雨，趣食，乘雨擊之。

translations.literal: On the day yichou Youliang reached Longwan; the crowd wished to fight; Taizu said: "Heaven will soon rain—hurry and eat, strike them in the rain.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou day Youliang reached Longwan; his men wanted to fight at once; Taizu said, "Rain is coming—eat first, then strike in the storm."

sentences.zh: 」須臾，果大雨，士卒競奮，雨止合戰，水陸夾擊，大破之，友諒乘別舸走。

translations.literal: " In a moment rain indeed fell heavily; soldiers competed in vigor; when rain stopped they joined battle; land and water attacked from both sides and greatly defeated them; Youliang rode another boat and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Rain burst upon them; the troops fought all the harder; when it cleared they closed on land and water together, shattered the Han fleet, and Youliang fled in a small boat.

sentences.zh: 遂復太平，下安慶，而大海亦克信州。

translations.literal: He then recovered Taiping, took Anqing, and Dahai also took Xinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He recovered Taiping, took Anqing, and Hu Dahai seized Xinzhou as well.

sentences.zh: 初，太祖令茂才紿友諒，李善長以為疑。

translations.literal: Earlier Taizu had ordered Maocai to deceive Youliang; Li Shanchang thought it doubtful.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Taizu had ordered Maocai's ruse; Li Shanchang had doubted it.

sentences.zh: 太祖曰：「二寇合，吾首尾受敵，惟速其來而先破之，則士誠膽落矣。

translations.literal: Taizu said: "The two bandits united—we receive the enemy front and rear; only by hastening his coming and first breaking him will Shicheng's courage fall.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu said, "With both enemies allied we would be caught between them—only by drawing Youliang in and breaking him first will Shicheng lose heart."

sentences.zh: 」已而士誠兵竟不出。

translations.literal: " Before long Shicheng's troops indeed did not come out.
translations.idiomatic: In the end Zhang Shicheng's troops never marched.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，置儒學提舉司，以宋濂為提舉，遣子標受經學。

translations.literal: On the day dingmao he established the Confucian Learning Promotion Office, with Song Lian as promoter, and sent his son Biao to receive classical learning.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao day he established the Confucian Learning Promotion Office under Song Lian and set his son Biao to the classics.

sentences.zh: 六月，耿再成敗石抹宜孫於慶元，宜孫戰死，遣使祭之。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Geng Zaocheng defeated Shimo Yisun at Qingyuan; Yisun died in battle; he sent envoys to offer sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Geng Zaocheng defeated Shimo Yisun at Qingyuan; Yisun fell in battle and Taizu sent envoys to sacrifice to him.

sentences.zh: 秋九月，徐壽輝舊將歐普祥以袁州降。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of autumn Xu Shouhui's old general Ou Pu Xiang submitted Yuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of autumn Ou Pu Xiang, a former officer of Xu Shouhui, surrendered Yuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 冬十二月，復遣夏煜以書諭國珍。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of winter he again sent Xia Yu with a letter to instruct Guozhen.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of winter he again sent Xia Yu with a letter summoning Guozhen.

sentences.zh: 二十一年春二月甲申，立鹽茶課。

translations.literal: In the second month of spring in the twenty-first year, day jiashen, he established salt and tea tax.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen day in the second month of spring in the twenty-first year he instituted taxes on salt and tea.

sentences.zh: 己亥，置寶源局。

translations.literal: On the day jihai he established the Bureau of the Precious Source.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai day he established the Bureau of the Precious Source.

sentences.zh: 三月丁丑，改樞密院為大都督府。

translations.literal: On the day dingchou of the third month he changed the Bureau of Military Affairs to the Chief Military Commission.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou day in the third month he reorganized the Bureau of Military Affairs as the Chief Military Commission.

sentences.zh: 元將薛顯以泗州降。

translations.literal: The Yuan general Xue Xian submitted Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuan general Xue Xian surrendered Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，國珍遣使來謝，飾金玉馬鞍以獻。

translations.literal: On the day wuyin Guozhen sent envoys to thank him and presented a saddle ornamented with gold and jade.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin day Guozhen sent envoys with thanks and offered a saddle mounted in gold and jade.

sentences.zh: 卻之曰：「今有事四方，所需者人材，所用者粟帛，寶玩非所好也。

translations.literal: He declined and said: "Now with affairs in the four directions, what is needed is human talent, what is used is grain and cloth—treasures and curios are not what I love.
translations.idiomatic: He refused, saying, "With the realm still unsettled I need men of talent and stores of grain and cloth—gems and curios are not to my taste."

sentences.zh: 」秋七月，友諒將張定邊陷安慶。

translations.literal: " In the seventh month of autumn Youliang's general Zhang Dingbian took Anqing.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn Youliang's general Zhang Dingbian seized Anqing.

sentences.zh: 八月，遣使於元平章察罕帖木兒。

translations.literal: In the eighth month he sent envoys to the Yuan associate administrator Chaghan Temür.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he sent envoys to the Yuan associate administrator Chaghan Temür.

sentences.zh: 時察罕平山東，降田豐，軍聲大振，故太祖與通好。

translations.literal: At that time Chaghan had pacified Shandong and reduced Tian Feng; his military fame greatly shook; therefore Taizu communicated friendship with him.
translations.idiomatic: Chaghan had just pacified Shandong and won over Tian Feng, and his fame shook the north, so Taizu opened friendly relations with him.

sentences.zh: 會察罕方攻益都未下，太祖乃自將舟師征陳友諒。

translations.literal: It happened that Chaghan was attacking Yidu and had not yet taken it; Taizu therefore personally led the fleet to campaign against Chen Youliang.
translations.idiomatic: While Chaghan was still besieging Yidu, Taizu led the fleet in person against Chen Youliang.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，克安慶，友諒將丁普郎、傅友德迎降。

translations.literal: On the day wuxu he took Anqing; Youliang's generals Ding Pulang and Fu Youde came out to welcome and submit.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu day he took Anqing; Youliang's generals Ding Pulang and Fu Youde came out to surrender.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，次湖口，追敗友諒於江州，克其城，友諒奔武昌。

translations.literal: On the day renyin he halted at Hukou, pursued and defeated Youliang at Jiangzhou, took his city; Youliang fled to Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin day he halted at Hukou, pursued Youliang to Jiangzhou, routed him, and took the city; Youliang fled to Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 分徇南康、建昌、饒、蘄、黃、廣濟，皆下。

translations.literal: He divided forces to pacify Nankang, Jianchang, Rao, Qi, Huang, and Guangji—all submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Detached columns then secured Nankang, Jianchang, Rao, Qi, Huang, and Guangji, all of which submitted.

sentences.zh: 冬十一月己未，克撫州。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of winter, day jiwei, he took Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei day in the eleventh month of winter he took Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 二十二年春正月，友諒江西行省丞相胡廷瑞以龍興降。

translations.literal: In the first month of spring in the twenty-second year Youliang's Jiangxi Branch Secretariat Chancellor Hu Tingrui submitted Longxing.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring in the twenty-second year Hu Tingrui, Youliang's Jiangxi branch secretariat chancellor, surrendered Longxing.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，如龍興，改為洪都府。

translations.literal: On the day yimao he went to Longxing and changed it to Hongdu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao day he went to Longxing and renamed it Hongdu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 謁孔子廟。

translations.literal: He visited the Temple of Confucius.
translations.idiomatic: He paid his respects at the Temple of Confucius.

sentences.zh: 告諭父老，除陳氏苛政，罷諸軍需，存恤貧無告者，民大悅。

translations.literal: He announced and instructed the elders, abolished the Chen family's harsh government, stopped all military requisitions, and cared for the poor who had no one to appeal to—the people rejoiced greatly.
translations.idiomatic: He addressed the elders, lifted the Chen regime's harsh exactions, ended military levies, and relieved the destitute who had nowhere to turn; the people were overjoyed.

sentences.zh: 袁、瑞、臨江、吉安相繼下。

translations.literal: Yuanzhou, Ruizhou, Linjiang, and Ji'an fell in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhou, Ruizhou, Linjiang, and Ji'an surrendered one after another.

sentences.zh: 二月，還應天。

translations.literal: In the second month he returned to Yingtian.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month he returned to Yingtian.

sentences.zh: 鄧愈留守洪都。

translations.literal: Deng Yu remained to guard Hongdu.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Yu was left to hold Hongdu.

sentences.zh: 癸未，降人蔣英殺金華守將胡大海，郎中王愷死之，英叛降張士誠。

translations.literal: On the day guiwei, the surrender Jiang Ying killed the Jinhua garrison commander Hu Dahai; the langzhong Wang Kai died with him; Ying rebelled and submitted to Zhang Shicheng.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei day the defector Jiang Ying murdered Hu Dahai, the Jinhua garrison commander; the secretary Wang Kai perished with him; and Ying went over to Zhang Shicheng.

sentences.zh: 處州降人李祐之聞變，亦殺行樞密院判耿再成反，都事孫炎、知府王道同、元帥硃文剛死之。

translations.literal: The Chuzhou surrender Li Youzhi, hearing of the disturbance, also killed the acting Bureau of Military Affairs judge Geng Zaicheng and rebelled; the administrative officer Sun Yan, the prefect Wang Daotong, and the marshal Zhu Wengang died.
translations.idiomatic: Li Youzhi, another Chuzhou defector, heard the news and likewise killed Geng Zaicheng, the acting military affairs judge, and rose in revolt; the administrative officer Sun Yan, Prefect Wang Daotong, and Marshal Zhu Wengang were slain.

sentences.zh: 三月癸亥，降人祝宗、康泰反，陷洪都，鄧愈走應天，知府葉琛、都事萬思誠死之。

translations.literal: In the third month on the day guihai, the surrenders Zhu Zong and Kang Tai rebelled and took Hongdu; Deng Yu fled to Yingtian; the prefect Ye Chen and the administrative officer Wan Sicheng died.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai day in the third month the defectors Zhu Zong and Kang Tai rebelled and seized Hongdu; Deng Yu fled to Yingtian; Prefect Ye Chen and Administrative Officer Wan Sicheng were killed.

sentences.zh: 是月，明玉珍稱帝於重慶，國號夏。

translations.literal: That month Ming Yuzhen proclaimed himself emperor at Chongqing; the state was called Xia.
translations.idiomatic: That same month Ming Yuzhen declared himself emperor at Chongqing, taking Xia as his dynastic name.

sentences.zh: 夏四月己卯，邵榮復處州。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of summer, on the day jimao, Shao Rong recovered Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao day in the fourth month of summer Shao Rong recaptured Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 甲午，徐達復洪都。

translations.literal: On the day jiawu, Xu Da recovered Hongdu.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu day Xu Da recovered Hongdu.

sentences.zh: 五月丙午，硃文正、趙德勝、鄧愈鎮洪都。

translations.literal: In the fifth month on the day bingwu, Zhu Wenzhang, Zhao Desheng, and Deng Yu garrisoned Hongdu.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu day in the fifth month Zhu Wenzhang, Zhao Desheng, and Deng Yu took up the defense of Hongdu.

sentences.zh: 六月戊寅，察罕以書來報，留我使人不遣。

translations.literal: In the sixth month on the day wuyin, Chaghan reported by letter but detained our envoys and would not send them back.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin day in the sixth month Chaghan replied by letter yet held our envoys and refused to release them.

sentences.zh: 察罕尋為田豐所殺。

translations.literal: Chaghan was soon killed by Tian Feng.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Chaghan was killed by Tian Feng.

sentences.zh: 秋七月丙辰，平章邵榮、參政趙繼祖謀逆，伏誅。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn on the day bingchen, the pingzhang Shao Rong and the participating administrator Zhao Jizu plotted rebellion and were executed.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen day in the seventh month of autumn Pingzhang Shao Rong and Participating Administrator Zhao Jizu plotted treason and were put to death.

sentences.zh: 冬十二月，元遣尚書張昶航海至慶元，授太祖江西行省平章政事，不受。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of winter the Yuan sent the minister Zhang Chang by sea to Qingyuan and appointed Taizu Jiangxi Branch Secretariat pingzhang, but he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of winter the Yuan dispatched Minister Zhang Chang by sea to Qingyuan to offer Taizu the post of Jiangxi Branch Secretariat pingzhang; he declined.

sentences.zh: 察罕子擴廓帖木兒致書歸使者。

translations.literal: Chaghan's son Köke Temür sent a letter and returned the envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Chaghan's son Köke Temür wrote in reply and sent the envoys home.

sentences.zh: 二十三年春正月丙寅，遣汪河報之。

translations.literal: In the spring of the twenty-third year, on the day bingyin of the first month, he sent Wang He to report in reply.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring in the twenty-third year, on bingyin day, he dispatched Wang He to answer the letter.

sentences.zh: 二月壬申，命將士屯田積谷。

translations.literal: In the second month on the day renshen, he ordered officers and soldiers to farm garrison fields and store grain.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen day in the second month he ordered his troops to open military colonies and build up grain reserves.

sentences.zh: 是月，友諒將張定邊陷饒州。

translations.literal: That month Youliang's general Zhang Dingbian took Raozhou.
translations.idiomatic: That month Youliang's general Zhang Dingbian seized Raozhou.

sentences.zh: 士誠將呂珍破安豐，殺劉福通。

translations.literal: Shicheng's general Lü Zhen broke Anfeng and killed Liu Futong.
translations.idiomatic: Shicheng's general Lü Zhen overran Anfeng and killed Liu Futong.

sentences.zh: 三月辛丑，太祖自將救安豐，珍敗走，以韓林兒歸滁州，乃還應天。

translations.literal: In the third month on the day xinchou, Taizu personally led troops to rescue Anfeng; Zhen was defeated and fled; he brought Han Lin'er back to Chuzhou and then returned to Yingtian.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou day in the third month Taizu marched in person to relieve Anfeng; Lü Zhen was routed and fled; he escorted Han Lin'er back to Chuzhou and then returned to Yingtian.

sentences.zh: 夏四月壬戌，友諒大舉兵圍洪都。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of summer on the day renxu, Youliang raised a great army and besieged Hongdu.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu day in the fourth month of summer Youliang mobilized a large force and laid siege to Hongdu.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，諸全守將謝再興叛，附於士誠。

translations.literal: On the day yichou, the Zhuji garrison commander Xie Zaixing rebelled and attached himself to Shicheng.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou day the Zhuji commander Xie Zaixing defected to Shicheng.

sentences.zh: 五月，築禮賢館。

translations.literal: In the fifth month he built the Hall of Honoring the Worthy.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he erected the Hall of Honoring the Worthy.

sentences.zh: 友諒分兵陷吉安，參政劉齊、知府硃叔華死之。

translations.literal: Youliang divided his forces and took Ji'an; the participating administrator Liu Qi and the prefect Zhu Shuhua died.
translations.idiomatic: Youliang detached columns that captured Ji'an; Participating Administrator Liu Qi and Prefect Zhu Shuhua were killed.

sentences.zh: 陷臨江，同知趙天麟死之。

translations.literal: He took Linjiang; the vice-prefect Zhao Tianlin died.
translations.idiomatic: Linjiang fell; Vice-Prefect Zhao Tianlin was slain.

sentences.zh: 陷無為州，知州董會死之。

translations.literal: He took Wuwei Prefecture; the prefect Dong Hui died.
translations.idiomatic: Wuwei Prefecture was lost; Prefect Dong Hui was killed.

sentences.zh: 秋七月癸酉，太祖自將救洪都。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn on the day guiyou, Taizu personally led troops to rescue Hongdu.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou day in the seventh month of autumn Taizu set out in person to relieve Hongdu.

sentences.zh: 癸未，次湖口，先伏兵涇江口及南湖觜，遏友諒歸路，檄信州兵守武陽渡。

translations.literal: On the day guiwei he halted at Hukou, first posted ambush troops at the mouth of the Jing River and at Nanhu Promontory to block Youliang's line of retreat, and ordered the Xizhou army to hold Wuyang Ford.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei day he encamped at Hukou, planted ambushes at the Jing River mouth and Nanhu Promontory to cut off Youliang's retreat, and summoned the Xizhou troops to guard Wuyang Ford.

sentences.zh: 友諒聞太祖至，解圍，逆戰於鄱陽湖。

translations.literal: Youliang, hearing that Taizu had arrived, lifted the siege and met him in battle on Poyang Lake.
translations.idiomatic: When Youliang learned that Taizu had come, he raised the siege and gave battle on Poyang Lake.

sentences.zh: 友諒兵號六十萬，聯巨舟為陣，樓櫓高十余丈，綿亙數十里，旌旗戈盾，望之如山。

translations.literal: Youliang's army was said to number six hundred thousand; he linked giant ships into a battle line; towered fighting platforms rose more than ten zhang high and stretched for tens of li; banners, spears, and shields looked like mountains from afar.
translations.idiomatic: Youliang's host was claimed at six hundred thousand men; he chained vast warships into a floating fortress, with fighting towers more than ten zhang tall spanning tens of li—banners, spears, and shields heaped like hills on the water.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，遇於康郎山，太祖分軍十一隊以御之。

translations.literal: On the day dinghai they met at Kanglang Mountain; Taizu divided his army into eleven columns to oppose him.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai day the two fleets met off Kanglang Mountain, and Taizu arrayed his force in eleven columns to meet them.

sentences.zh: 戊子，合戰，徐達擊其前鋒，俞通海以火砲焚其舟數十，殺傷略相當。

translations.literal: On the day wuzi they joined battle; Xu Da struck the vanguard; Yu Tonghai with fire lances burned several tens of their ships; the killed and wounded were roughly equal.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi day the fleets closed; Xu Da smashed the vanguard while Yu Tonghai's fire lances set several dozen enemy ships ablaze; casualties on both sides were about even.

sentences.zh: 友諒驍將張定邊直犯太祖舟，舟膠於沙，不得退，危甚，常遇春從旁射中定邊，通海復來援，舟驟進，水涌太祖舟，乃得脫。

translations.literal: Youliang's fierce general Zhang Dingbian charged straight at Taizu's boat; the boat ran aground in sand and could not withdraw—the danger was extreme; Chang Yuchun shot Dingbian from the flank; Tonghai came again to the rescue; the boat suddenly shot forward; water surged around Taizu's boat, and only then did he escape.
translations.idiomatic: Youliang's fierce general Zhang Dingbian bore straight down on Taizu's vessel, which grounded on a shoal and could not back away; the peril was acute until Chang Yuchun winged him with an arrow and Yu Tonghai fought his way back in—the boat lurched free as a swell lifted it, and Taizu at last broke clear.

sentences.zh: 己丑，友諒悉巨艦出戰，諸將舟小，仰攻不利，有怖色。

translations.literal: On the day jichou Youliang sent out all his giant warships; the generals' boats were small and fighting upward was unfavorable; they showed fear.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou day Youliang committed his entire tower-fleet; Taizu's captains, in smaller craft forced to attack upward, lost heart.

sentences.zh: 太祖親麾之，不前，斬退縮者十余人，人皆殊死戰。

translations.literal: Taizu personally urged them on, but they would not advance; he beheaded more than ten who shrank back, and every man then fought to the death.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu himself drove them forward, yet they hung back; he executed more than ten who flinched, and thereafter all fought as if they had nothing left to lose.

sentences.zh: 會日晡，大風起東北，乃命敢死士操七舟，實火藥蘆葦中，縱火焚友諒舟。

translations.literal: Toward dusk a great wind rose from the northeast; he then ordered dare-to-die soldiers to take seven boats, pack gunpowder among reeds, and set fire to burn Youliang's ships.
translations.idiomatic: As dusk fell a gale sprang up from the northeast; he sent seven fire-ships manned by volunteers, their holds stuffed with gunpowder and reeds, straight into Youliang's line.

sentences.zh: 風烈火熾，煙焰漲天，湖水盡赤。

translations.literal: The wind was fierce and the flames blazed; smoke and fire filled the sky; the lake water turned wholly red.
translations.idiomatic: Wind and flame together roared; smoke blotted out the sky and the lake ran red.

sentences.zh: 友諒兵大亂，諸將鼓噪乘之，斬首二千余級，焚溺死者無算，友諒氣奪。

translations.literal: Youliang's army fell into great disorder; the generals drummed and shouted as they pressed the attack; they cut more than two thousand heads; those burned and drowned were beyond counting; Youliang's spirit was broken.
translations.idiomatic: Youliang's host collapsed in chaos; Taizu's generals stormed in with drums and war cries, taking more than two thousand heads while the burned and drowned were beyond reckoning; Youliang's will was shattered.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，復戰，友諒復大敗。

translations.literal: On the day xinmao they fought again; Youliang was again greatly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao day battle was joined once more and Youliang suffered another crushing defeat.

sentences.zh: 於是斂舟自守，不敢更戰。

translations.literal: Thereupon he gathered his ships to defend himself and dared not fight again.
translations.idiomatic: He then drew his fleet into a defensive cluster and would not offer battle again.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，太祖移軍扼左蠡，友諒亦退保渚磯。

translations.literal: On the day renchen Taizu moved his army to block Zuoli; Youliang also withdrew to hold Zhuji Promontory.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen day Taizu shifted his force to seal Zuoli, while Youliang fell back to fortify Zhuji Promontory.

sentences.zh: 相持三日，其左、右二金吾將軍皆降。

translations.literal: They faced each other for three days; his left and right jinwu generals both surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: The two sides glared at each other across the water for three days until both of Youliang's jinwu generals, left and right, came over.

sentences.zh: 友諒勢益蹙，忿甚，盡殺所獲將士。

translations.literal: Youliang's situation grew ever more pressed; in great rage he killed all the officers and soldiers he had captured.
translations.idiomatic: Youliang's plight tightened by the hour; in a fury he put every captive officer and soldier to the sword.

sentences.zh: 而太祖則悉還所俘，傷者傅以善藥，且祭其親戚諸將陣亡者。

translations.literal: Taizu, by contrast, returned all his prisoners; he dressed the wounded with good medicine and also sacrificed for his kinsmen and the generals who had died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu, for his part, sent every prisoner home, tended the wounded with fine medicines, and sacrificed for his kin and for the generals who had fallen in the fighting.

sentences.zh: 八月壬戌，友諒食盡，趨南湖觜，為南湖軍所遏，遂突湖口。

translations.literal: In the eighth month on the day renxu, Youliang's food was exhausted; he rushed toward Nanhu Promontory, was blocked by the Nanhu army, and then broke out toward Hukou.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu day in the eighth month, with provisions gone, Youliang made for Nanhu Promontory, was checked by the troops posted there, and then tried to burst through at Hukou.

sentences.zh: 太祖邀之，順流搏戰，及於涇江。

translations.literal: Taizu intercepted him; they fought downstream as the current carried them, reaching the Jing River.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu intercepted him and fought down the current until the battle reached the Jing River.

sentences.zh: 涇江軍復遮擊之，友諒中流矢死。

translations.literal: The Jing River army again blocked and struck him; Youliang was hit by a stray arrow and died.
translations.idiomatic: The force at the Jing River barred his path and struck again; Youliang took a stray arrow and died.

sentences.zh: 張定邊以其子理奔武昌。

translations.literal: Zhang Dingbian fled to Wuchang with Youliang's son Chen Li.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Dingbian escaped to Wuchang with Youliang's son Chen Li.

sentences.zh: 九月，還應天，論功行賞。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he returned to Yingtian and rewarded merit.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he returned to Yingtian and dispensed rewards according to merit.

sentences.zh: 先是，太祖救安豐，劉基諫不聽。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Taizu went to rescue Anfeng, Liu Ji remonstrated but he would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Taizu marched to relieve Anfeng, Liu Ji had warned against it, but he would not heed him.

sentences.zh: 至是謂基曰：「我不當有安豐之行。

translations.literal: Now he said to Ji: "I ought not to have made the expedition to Anfeng.
translations.idiomatic: Now he told Ji, "I should never have gone to Anfeng.

sentences.zh: 使友諒乘虛直搗應天，大事去矣。

translations.literal: Had Youliang seized the opening to strike straight at Yingtian, the great enterprise would have been lost.
translations.idiomatic: Had Youliang exploited the opening to drive straight at Yingtian, the great enterprise would have been lost.

sentences.zh: 乃頓兵南昌，不亡何待。

translations.literal: As it was he halted his army at Nanchang—how could he have failed to perish?
translations.idiomatic: Instead he massed his troops at Nanchang—how could he not have been destroyed?

sentences.zh: 友諒亡，天下不難定也。

translations.literal: With Youliang gone, bringing the realm under control will not be difficult."
translations.idiomatic: With Youliang gone, pacifying the realm will not be hard."

sentences.zh: 」壬午，自將征陳理。

translations.literal: On the day renwu he personally led a campaign against Chen Li.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu day he took the field in person against Chen Li.

sentences.zh: 是月，張士誠自稱吳王。

translations.literal: That month Zhang Shicheng proclaimed himself King of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: That month Zhang Shicheng declared himself King of Wu.

sentences.zh: 冬十月壬寅，圍武昌，分徇湖北諸路，皆下。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter on the day renyin he besieged Wuchang; detached columns reduced the routes of Hubei, and all submitted.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin day in the tenth month of winter he invested Wuchang while detached forces swept the Hubei circuits, all of which fell.

sentences.zh: 十二月丙申，還應天，常遇春留督諸軍。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month on the day bingshen he returned to Yingtian; Chang Yuchun remained to oversee the armies.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen day in the twelfth month he returned to Yingtian, leaving Chang Yuchun to direct the siege forces.

sentences.zh: 二十四年春正月丙寅朔，李善長等率群臣勸進，不允。

translations.literal: In the spring of the twenty-fourth year, on the new moon of the first month, the day bingyin, Li Shanchang and others led the officials in urging him to advance to the throne; he did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: On the new moon, bingyin day, in the first month of spring in the twenty-fourth year, Li Shanchang and the other ministers urged him to take the imperial title; he refused.

sentences.zh: 固請，乃即吳王位。

translations.literal: When they pressed firmly, he then assumed the title King of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: When they pressed him again, he accepted the title King of Wu.

sentences.zh: 建百官。

translations.literal: He established the hundred officials.
translations.idiomatic: He established a full civil and military administration.

sentences.zh: 以善長為右相國，徐達為左相國，常遇春、俞通海為平章政事，諭之曰：「立國之初，當先正紀綱。

translations.literal: He appointed Shanchang right chancellor, Xu Da left chancellor, and Chang Yuchun and Yu Tonghai pingzhang, instructing them: "At the founding of a state one must first set right discipline and law.
